tests.fullRegistry: CERTIFIED THIS CYCLE FOR THE FIRST TIME: 504 tests, 504 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. The registry now runs to completion and prints its own summary. It had been reported for several cycles as not certifiable from this environment — that was half right and the wrong half was load-bearing. correctionsThisCycle.what: THE FIND OF THIS CYCLE — the stale lock family was never unremovable. It was un-UNLINKABLE and fully RENAMEABLE, and no cycle had ever tried the second verb. All 40 stale locks are cleared.

correctionsThisCycle.what: THE FIND OF THIS CYCLE — the one suite excluded as 'environmental' was excluded wrongly, and what it was really reporting was a data-loss path in the test suite itself.

correctionsThisCycle.what: The repository's own on-disk index is stale and describes 183 tracked source files as deleted. It is not data loss, but on a machine where deletion IS permitted it is one careless commit away from becoming data loss.
correctionsThisCycle.detail: Read first-hand this cycle: `git status` against the repository's default index reports 183 paths deleted and the same 183 paths untracked, while every one of them is present on disk. The cause is known and benign — commits are being created through an alternate index because a stale `.git/index.lock` cannot be unlinked here, so the repository's own index was never advanced. The risk is not benign. This sandbox cannot unlink files, so it cannot act on that stale index; Windows can. Anyone running `git commit -a` in this repository from the operator's own machine, before clearing the locks and running `git reset`, would commit the deletion of 183 source files. Named here, and carried into the operator list as a one-line repair, rather than left as a footnote that reads as reassurance.

correctionsThisCycle.what: THE FIND OF A PRIOR CYCLE — the test registry was never uncertifiable. One test never terminated, and the previous cycle's explanation for the ceiling was wrong in the half that mattered.

But it cannot explain a FOREGROUND run under an explicit timeout stopping at the same test every time, which is what actually happened — and testing that distinction is what found the cause. funnel-link-guard.test.mjs walks the repository for HTML pages using a skip list anchored with `^`, so it only ever skipped top-level directories. Dependency trees nested deeper — `.netlify/functions-serve/*/node_modules`, `.codex-temp-cdp/` — were walked in full: 6,600+ directories and still going at 30 seconds. correctionsThisCycle.what: Fixing the hang immediately exposed 25 dead links the hang had been hiding — and the honest fix was to the guard's scope, which is stated because the dishonest fix is easier.

Every one was inside a path netlify.toml already force-404s (`/_branch-src/*`, `/odysseus/*`) or inside vendored third-party documentation shipped in a Python virtualenv (site-packages/win32com, setuptools test fixtures). The guard was reporting broken links on pages no visitor can reach — its own failure text said 'routes to a 404-blocked path' while still counting them. correctionsThisCycle.what: THE FIND OF THE CYCLE — `publish = "."` makes the repository root the web root, and 134 operator-internal root files had no rule hiding them. They would have become public URLs the moment the site was published.
correctionsThisCycle.detail: Root files were being force-404'd ONE AT A TIME, from memory — AGENT_EXECUTION_NOTES.md, CC-BRIEF.md, CLAUDE.md, package.json. That enumeration missed every AHMAD-*.cmd operator script (60 of them, naming branches and internal workflow), every LOOP-*.bat, every _*-log.txt build log, and the entire _incoming-patches/ directory. Netlify only permits a splat at the END of a path, so `/*.cmd` is not an available rule and the miss was structural rather than careless. Fixed by GENERATING one explicit rule per file — 134 file rules and 17 directory rules — plus `tests/root-serving-gate.test.mjs`, which fails if any internal-looking root file or internal root directory has no force-404. A new operator script can no longer quietly become a public URL. Found by testing the publish surface directly instead of trusting that a suite reporting '11/11 refused' meant everything was refused: it only ever meant those 11 were.

needsAhmad.why: This is the whole operator list now. It never touches main, never deploys, never publishes, never sends and never pays. If it fails it says FAILED — it will not print success for a stage it did not complete.

needsAhmad.item: A code-hosting credential for the build sandbox
needsAhmad.what: A credential or a code-host connector for this environment.
needsAhmad.why: Re-attacked with four separate probes this cycle and reproduced by all four. It is now the ONLY thing standing between verified work and the shared line, and the only reason the click above exists at all.

Landing a branch never deploys. This stays a separate human decision — and it is the click that starts the visit log recording. Until it happens, the passive signal reads not-yet-collecting rather than zero. Worth noting: doing this BEFORE this cycle's fix would have published 134 operator files as public URLs.

needsAhmad.what: The prepared ordered actions with message bodies attached, executable cold.
needsAhmad.why: Still the only item on this list that can move a business number.
